Even carbonite.''"<br />"''It sounds&hellip;dreadfully crude. And painful.|Palpatine and Mace Windu|<ref name="Shatterpoint">[[Shatterpoint (novel)|''Shatterpoint'']]</ref>}}
[[File:Mace Windu SWI38.png|thumb|right|200px|Jedi Master Mace Windu had experience with dead blades.]]
'''Dead blade''' was a term used by [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] for any non-energized non-powered [[Melee weapon/Legends|melee weapon]], typically taking the form of a sharp blade made of such substances as [[Metal/Legends|metal]], [[Ceramic/Legends|ceramic]], [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]], and [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]]; examples included simple [[Knife/Legends|knives]] and [[Axe/Legends|axes]].<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|175|dead blade}}</ref> This was in direct contrast to [[Weapon/Legends|weapons]] such as [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]], which were in essence entirely energized, and [[Vibroblade/Legends|vibroblades]], which were characterized by their energized vibration, thus making them more effective at cutting through various substances.<ref name="Shatterpoint" />

[[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] was familiar with the appearance of wounds inflicted by dead blades.<ref name="Shatterpoint" /> In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="Date">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of [[Shatterpoint (novel)|''Shatterpoint'']] to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].</ref> while reviewing a [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Haruun Kal/Legends|Haruun Kal]] with [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], and a [[Republic Intelligence/Legends|Republic Intelligence]] [[Agent/Legends|agent]], Windu identified several such marks on a [[Death/Legends|corpse]] seen in the image. Palpatine expressed distaste at the idea of a dead blade, considering it a crude device with a painful application.  Windu noted that cuts made with such a weapon did not always hurt.<ref name="Shatterpoint" />

==Behind the scenes==
The expression "dead blade" first appeared in the novel [[Shatterpoint (novel)|''Shatterpoint'']], which was written by [[Matthew Stover]] and published in [[2003]].<ref name="Shatterpoint"/>
